item.title: Social Bias in LLM-Generated Code: Benchmark and Mitigation
item.description:
The problem of social bias in Large Language Models (LLMs) is addressed using a benchmark of 343 real-world coding tasks, and the authors evaluate four prominent LLMs. The authors find severe bias across all models, with Code Bias Scores reaching up to 60.58%.

IT Breakdown: This research can be applied in IT operations to identify and mitigate social bias in AI-generated code, which can be used to develop more fair and inclusive software applications. To package this as an AI automation service, UK SMBs can use the SocialBias-Bench benchmark to evaluate their own AI models and develop strategies to reduce bias in their code.

item.title: When RAG Chatbots Expose Their Backend: An Anonymized Case Study of Privacy and Security Risks in Patient-Facing Medical AI
item.description:
The specific problem addressed is the security and privacy risks of patient-facing medical chatbots based on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), using a method that involves a two-stage strategy for assessment. The authors aim to report an anonymized, non-destructive security assessment of a publicly accessible patient-facing medical RAG chatbot and identify governance lessons for safe deployment of generative AI in health.

IT Breakdown: The specific practical application of this research in IT operations or helpdesk context is the assessment of security and privacy risks in patient-facing medical chatbots. This could be packaged as an AI automation service for a UK SMB client by offering security assessments and governance lessons for safe deployment of generative AI in healthcare.
